findings.failure_scenario: `import agents` executes `agents/__init__.py` -> `_config.py` (`from .tracing import set_tracing_export_api_key`) -> `tracing/__init__.py` (`from .create import ...`) -> `create.py:7` (`from .setup import GLOBAL_TRACE_PROVIDER`) -> `setup.py:10` (`from . import util`) -> `util.py:1`, which requests `GLOBAL_TRACE_PROVIDER` from the still-partially-initialized `setup` module (the name is assigned only at setup.py:232, after line 10). Python raises `ImportError: cannot import name 'GLOBAL_TRACE_PROVIDER' from partially initialized module 'agents.tracing.setup' (most likely due to a circular import)`, so the entire library fails to import. The baseline util.py imported only stdlib modules, so this cycle did not exist before the change.
findings.summary: The new `from .setup import GLOBAL_TRACE_PROVIDER` in util.py creates a circular import with setup.py's `from . import util`, so importing the agents package raises ImportError.

findings.failure_scenario: A user calls `set_trace_provider(custom_provider)` to install a provider with custom processors or a disabled state, then calls `trace('wf')` or `add_trace_processor(p)`. `create.trace()` and the package helpers still use the default provider: the custom provider's processors never receive spans, `set_tracing_disabled(True)` after the swap keeps mutating the old provider, and the `atexit`-registered `GLOBAL_TRACE_PROVIDER.shutdown` (tracing/__init__.py:114) flushes the default provider's processors, silently dropping the custom provider's buffered traces on exit.
findings.summary: set_trace_provider() cannot take effect: every consumer (util.py:1, create.py:7, tracing/__init__.py:21) bound GLOBAL_TRACE_PROVIDER at import time, so rebinding the name in setup.py leaves them calling the original default TraceProvider.

findings.failure_scenario: A subclass `class MyProvider(TraceProvider)` overrides `gen_trace_id` to return a custom ID format (the extensibility point this change adds at setup.py:127-137), then calls `MyProvider().create_trace('wf')` or installs it via `set_trace_provider`. The generated trace still gets the default `trace_<uuid>` ID because create_trace routes through the global util path (setup.py:154; likewise traces.py:141 and spans.py:181 for span IDs), so the override is silently ignored and the new instance methods are dead code for the default flow.
findings.summary: create_trace still calls the module-level util.gen_trace_id() instead of the newly added self.gen_trace_id(), so the TraceProvider instance methods added by this change are never used by the provider's own trace/span creation.
